title: Azure Disk Storage - Simply Explained

entities.name: Azure Disk Storage
entities.quote: most people don't fully understand, as your disk storage, it's the virtual hard drive for your cloud VMs

entities.name: Microsoft Azure
entities.quote: When you create a VM in Azure, it automatically creates an OSDisk.

quotes.text: The trick is matching the disk to what your workload actually needs, so you're not over-provisioning and wasting cash, nor under-provisioning and getting slow performance.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core sizing principle of the episode.

quotes.text: With premium SSD V2, you can independently adjust capacity, IOPS and throughput. No downtime, no disk swaps, just change the settings and it happens.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the defining advantage of Premium SSD v2.

quotes.text: If you're not running SAP HANA or a trading platform or something extreme, you don't need ultra-disk. Start with premium SSDV2 only move to ultra if your monitoring shows you need it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical recommendation that avoids overspending on Ultra Disk.

quotes.text: Match the disk type to your workload. Not the other way around. Don't buy ultra-disk because it sounds impressive.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable bottom line for choosing disk types.

chapters.title: Intro: the virtual hard drive for VMs

takeaways: IOPS, throughput and latency determine disk performance, and the goal is to match them to the workload without over- or under-provisioning.
Premium SSD v2 decouples capacity, IOPS and throughput and covers most production databases at a lower price than Ultra Disk.
Ultra Disk is reserved for extreme workloads such as SAP HANA or trading platforms, while Standard SSD is enough for dev/test and low-traffic servers.
hook: Every Azure VM needs disk storage, and the wrong tier means either overpaying or slow performance. This episode explains Standard SSD, Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disk for Azure beginners and admins, with a simple decision guide and cost tips.
